newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat tax bids total 220,000 tonnes -traders.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat tax bids total 220,000 tonnes -traders.

text.p: Exporters bid through France for approximately 220,000 tonnes of European Union wheat with taxes instead of refunds, grain traders said on Thursday.

They also reported heavy bidding of between 700,000 and 800,000 tonnes for refunds at zero Ecus, using a technicality which allows holders of such licences to collect up to four Ecus per tonne in subsidy between August and November.
French grain office ONIC earlier reported total bids for 1.13 million tonnes spread between taxes of 0.14 to two Ecus and refunds of zero to 14.99 Ecus.
Traders can send in bids with both refunds and taxes, but the Commission generally grants one or the other, not both.
A refund of zero is a future investment since it comes with storage aid of one Ecu per month between August and the maximum validity date of end-November.
Taxed export licences are valid for the same period but do not come with the monthly increment.
